item.title: DFRA - All About You EP
item.description: Label: Groovin Records | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: House , Jazz House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Groovin Records

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: House , Jazz House

Argentinian deep house maestro DFRA returns to Groovin Recordings while still riding high off the success of his other project, the DFRA Experience Jazz Band, for a second 12". Where his debut leaned heavily into live modal jazz and bebop structures woven through electronic production, this follow-up finds him pivot back toward the late-night dancefloor and just in time for some mid-summer heat. A masterclass in clean, sophisticated deep house, the Buenos Aires producer pairs crisp percussion with warm, hypnotic basslines and soulful chord work throughout. From the vocal-tinged groove of the title track to the moodier late-night cuts on the flip, this one strikes a rare balance between classic and modern.

  • A1. All About You
  • A2. Late Night Coffee
  • B1. Subterfuge
  • B2. GUS

item.title: Omar S - Pain EP
item.description: Label: FXHE | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: House , Detroit House
item.content:encoded:
Label: FXHE

Prix: 22,00 €

Style: House , Detroit House

Omar S has always seemingly enjoyed working with other local talents and giving them a platform of his own vital FXHE label. That's what he does here as he looks to Motor City creatives in the young King Milo, Tayloe and old friend John F.M. He kicks off in solo mode with some signature stripped back house futurism on 'Tongue Pecker' before 'Pain' is a high speed and sleazy ghetto bumper. The standout is 'I Love Your Girl Friend' (feat John FM) with its heart aching vocal, gorgeous piano chords and deep, dusty drum bumps. A real classic in the making which is followed by another achingly beautiful mix of soulful vocals and grotty lo-fi synth and drums on 'Some Good Loving' (feat Tayloe).

Much like vital Detroit label Moods & Grooves, The Solid Gold Playaz are a beloved force in the house scene. They tragically lost their co-founder Kenny Gino in 2021, but by then had already assured the legacy with deep house grooves that exude funk and class. In honour of Kenny's memory, surviving member Mike Theus carries on the journey with a new EP that, across four tracks, demonstrates real unity. Each one is built on nice lo-fi dusty drums, with undercooked synth lines bringing the unusual soul, bass adding the all-important low-end interest and plenty of smart samples finishing in style.

Norm Talley's Upstairs Asylum is a contemporary Detroit house favourite. This latest 12" is an update of what's going on in the Motor City right now, with four local producers all coming correct. The inimitable Dez Andres kicks off with one of his smooth hip-hop inclined deep house jams with sunny melodies and hooky vocals, then DJ Ryte Nou sinks into a warm, cuddly house sound with a soulful vocal smudged into the mix on 'Aint Going No-Way.' Marcus Harris takes care of the flip with a pair of seriously vibes sounds - the first well swung and dubby, the second with a more expressive rhythm and big guitar licks adding some Balearic charm.

Old school and new school collide here as Mixmode Recordings boss and longtime deep house servant Delano Smith joins contemporary trailblazer Ash Lauryn on a seductive and smoky new single. Lauryn contributes a spoken word vocal that has her whispering into the mic with alluring late night intimacy as classic drums roll beneath dusty chords. Atlanta mainstay Kai Alce then brings his signature bounce and swing to a remix that has brighter chord work. On the flip is the meditative 'Let The Rhythm' with its swirling chords and subtle Detroit touches with another entrancing and conscious spoken word from Lauryn finishing it with style.

item.title: Greg Gow/Brian Kage - D Send To Ascend EP
item.description: Label: Michigander | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: Techno , Detroit Techno
item.content:encoded:

Style: Techno , Detroit Techno

The Michigander label is back with more straight business, this time pairing Greg Gow with Brian Kage for a four-tracker that deals in authentic Detroit vibes from two city mainstays. 'D Send To Ascend' opens up with a driving but deep sound that teeters between house and techno with foggy pads and monstrous bass. 'Depth Gauge' pulls back for a more swinging and roomy cut, but one that still has plenty of mass in the low end. 'Prophet Pulses' will get dancers up on their toes with a rumbling undercarriage and drums that subtly uplift as the chords work their soulful cosmic magic. 'Lines Crossed' shuts down with tight drums and loopy chords that keep you locked in the here and now.

  • B1. Prophet Pulses

item.title: Dream 2 Science - My Love Turns To Liquid
item.description: Label: Rush Hour | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Rush Hour

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

Way back in 2012, Rush Hour reissued Ben 'Cozmo D' Cenac and Gregg Fore's sole, self-titled album as Dream 2 Science - a glorious collection of heady deep house brilliance headed up by near perfect vocal number 'My Love Turns To Liquid'. Now they've returned to the duo's slim catalogue and reissued the 19909 12" version of that killer cut. The astonishingly good 'Original Mix' - the very same version showcased on the album - comes backed by a quartet of remixes and DJ tools. On side A you'll find the tactile, aquatic and subtly percussive, dub mix style 'Warm Water mix' and the synths-and-vocals 'Padapella'. Over on the reverse, Cenac doffs a cap to early UK bleep and bass and sub-heavy 1990 NYC deep house cuts on the superb 'Cozmic remix' and 'Cozmic remix instrumental'.

item.title: Various Artists - Strange Weather: A Different Kettle Of Fish (feat Housey Doingz, The Ron Honey Experience, Space Bunny)
item.description: Label: Sushitech | Prix: 50,00 € | Style: Tech House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Sushitech

Prix: 50,00 €

Style: Tech House

Laurant Webb, Dave Coker, Justin Bailey, and Dave Pine were the key figures behind Strange Weather Studios, which was a creative hub in Southeast London that helped shape the very early sound of tech house in the capital. Collaborating with friends and partners on several projects, they produced a number of influential records that defined the genre including under aliases such as Housey Doingz, 7th Voyage, and Space Bunny. This release on Sushitech, which always does a fine job of offering up the best tech house past and present, pays tribute to the studio and its collaborators with representative tracks carefully selected by Laurant Webb and label head Yossi Amoyal. Restored and remastered from rare DATs and pressed up to no fewer than six sides of vinyl, it's a great look at a significant moment in the evolution of tech house.

item.title: Teflon Dons/Coastal Commission - The Rendezvous ( Reissue)
item.description: Label: Pacific Coast House | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: House , Tech House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Pacific Coast House

Prix: 22,00 €

Style: House , Tech House

Sam Robson continues to reissue gems from the vaults of his initially short-lived Pacific Coast House Recordings imprint, which released a string of superb West Coast house singles between 1999 and 2003. This split 12" originally landed way back in 2001 and has become something of an in-demand rarity in recent years. The now-familiar Teflon Dons handle side A, wrapping jaunty, spaced-out stabs, intergalactic pads, echo-laden vocal snippets and TB-303 style moody electronics around a hybrid acid house/tech-house groove on the swirling and immersive early morning delights of 'Vice'. Over on side B, Robson dons his The Coastal Commission guise for a deeper, dub-flecked and breakbeat-enhanced house workout that adds cosmic spoken word snippets and effects-laden ambient chords to the San Fran deep house template drawn up by Dubtribe Soundsystem and Charles Webster.

Tracklist:

  • A1. The Coastal Commission - Our Music
  • B1. Teflon Dons - Vice

item.title: Dexter - Tangent Boy
item.description: Label: Endell Street | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: House , Tech House UK
item.content:encoded:
Label: Endell Street

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: House , Tech House UK

Dexter is a UK artist who has had plenty of say in shaping the sound of tech house over the years, and now he's back with some classics on Endell Street. Open 'Tangent Boy' has been something of a secret weapon amongst those who know for some time, despite never officially being out on vinyl, until now that is. It's got everything proper tech house should have - dub weight, irresistible swing, and crispy drums. On the flip, 'Funk Warped' is another seasoned favourite that has been remastered for this welcome return. It's punchier than the opener with a kinetic groove and some nice trippy synths. Class.

Tracklist:

  • A1. Tangent Boy
  • B1. Funk Warped
